articles.title: The vanity economy is taking over America’s downtowns
articles.summary: City streets and suburban shopping malls are being reshaped by our collective obsession with appearance, health and fitness.
articles.body:
QQ Nails opened its first salon in New York City twenty years ago. By 2020, QQ had grown to roughly 20 locations.

It's nearly doubled in size since the pandemic. Thirty-eight QQ salons now dot the city's streets, with plans for dozens more. In one six block radius in Manhattan, there are four.

"People are more willing to spend on self-care, self-expressiveness and these types of larger services," CEO Tian Jiang said.

Brick-and-mortar stores were once designed to sell you stuff: shoes, furniture and TVs. Today, they're all about making your face, abs, hair and nails look and feel fit for the world— both the in-person and social media versions of your life.

City streets and suburban shopping malls have been reconfigured in response to our collective obsession with appearance, health and performance. The transformation of retail storefronts is the physical manifestation of marketing buzzwords like " looksmaxxing ," "self-care" and "longevity."

Nail salons on every block. Med spas expanding rapidly. Pilates chains opening hundreds of clubs. High-intensity weightlifting studios, bathhouses, saunas, stretching studios, cryotherapy and IV therapy.

Nationwide, more than 1 out of every 4 retail leases signed in the United States this year has been from a cosmetics, beauty service or fitness company, according to CoStar. It's on pace to be the highest annual share on record.

Physical stores to help you look good online

The presence of screens everywhere helps explain the changes in the physical commercial landscape.

People want to look good when they see others in real life. They also want to look good on Instagram, Hinge and TikTok. Vanity businesses serve both our in-person and digital lives simultaneously.

"There is definitely 'aesthetic creep' that has intensified in recent years" Natalia Mehlman Petrzela, a historian of American politics and culture at The New School, said in an email. Women and gay men have long felt pressure to present themselves, but "straight men are now encompassed by the beauty-industrial complex in new ways" than the pre-looksmaxxing, social media era.

Physical retail has also changed because many younger consumers prioritize smaller acts of self-improvement in an economy where traditional life milestones such as homeownership, marriage and kids, feel out of reach. Increasingly living alone and staying single, these consumers are less willing to cut back on gym memberships and manicures that help them feel healthier, stronger and more attractive.

articles.title: Coffee giant Dutch Bros made all of its executives, including the CEO, do a two-week bootcamp where they learned how to pour drinks and run stores
articles.summary: Dutch Bros CEO Christine Barone and senior leaders have to complete six shifts of hands-on shop training, sharpening their hospitality skills and perfecting...
articles.body:
Dutch Bros CEO Christine Barone can do more than steer a $7.5 billion coffee chain—she can also hold her own behind the store counter. Like all other top leaders at the beverage giant, she embarked on a two-week bootcamp to learn the ropes of being a "broista." And the chain's workers weren't afraid to call her out on mistakes.

"As I trained, people knew I was the CEO, and our teams would always point out when I was doing something wrong," Barone tells Fortune. "That is one of the magical signs of a great culture that I need to make sure I build upon, because when my team cares so much about the customer that they're going to tell the CEO that they were doing something wrong, I love that."

The executive's beverage training is part of the company's "growth from within" model. Dutch Bros staffers, from store owners to senior managers, have been put through the course for years to understand the hard work of the chain's 25,000 broistas churning out drinks. During the training, leaders complete six shifts of hands-on shop training, sharpening their hospitality skills, perfecting drink orders, and learning how to deliver on the values of speed, quality and service.

The chain says they witness first-hand how customer connections are made, and learn how to perfect drinks including the popular Golden Eagle coffee, so that everything tastes the same on Monday as it does on Wednesday. At the end, Dutch Bros leaders have to pass a "Flow" test, with questions ranging from drink recipes and company history to shop operations and culture. And the brand is serious about its standards; those who don't pass have to retake the test.

Barone says the broista bootcamp reflects the vision of Dutch Bros' founders: brothers Travis Boersma and the late Dane Boersma, who named the company in honor of their grandparents who immigrated from the Netherlands. Aside from gaining technical and hospitality expertise, she says the training nurtures "compelling futures" at the company, and lights a path for employees to work themselves up the chain of command.

"As we rolled it out to the more broader team across HQ, we were very thoughtful about making sure our marketing teams went through the training, especially the folks who are helping to design and make beverages," the CEO explains. "Just thinking through: What are all those decisions we're making that touch where the customer interaction is? And how do we ensure that everyone who is designing programs for our teams, or designing marketing programs, or designing new beverages, really understands what the shop environment feels like?"

articles.title: What Intel Doubters Got Wrong
articles.summary: If you had been weighing Intel in early November 2025, the headlines were already split between a complex restructuring plan and questions about whether AI-f...
articles.body:
If you had been weighing Intel in early November 2025, the headlines were already split between a complex restructuring plan and questions about whether AI-focused partnerships could offset organizational drag. Holding Intel over the past year would have returned 47.6%, including dividends. If you were setting up a position on 2025-11-06, the real puzzle was how to balance hopes around AI and foundry deals with concerns about bureaucracy, execution and future profitability.

The move put Intel in the middle of this trade. Scan 53 AI infrastructure stocks for other companies exposed to it.

The Two Intel Stories Investors Were Arguing About

The shares cost US$37.24 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Intel then had to choose between a confident product revival story and a slower, restructuring heavy reset.

The bullish roadmap described a fair value of US$79, which reflected expectations of 10.0% revenue growth and a 22.0% profit margin over five years as new PC and data center chips rolled out.

The cautious restructuring view indicated a fair value of US$25.18, based on revenue rising 3.5% a year and profit margins reaching 7.8% while AI partnerships and foundry efforts were established.

What The Results Changed For The Intel Thesis

Intel's later quarters brought heavy AI contracts and partnerships, yet the cleanest test of the original debate came from the Q3 2026 figures. Revenue reached US$16,513m versus US$13,653m a year earlier, but net income slipped to US$3,320m and net margin moved from 29.8% to 20.1%. That mix of higher sales and weaker profitability cut both ways for the bullish and cautious cases.

The whole episode turned on one assumption that applies well beyond Intel. Hopes around product revivals and AI exposure still needed margins to hold up. When you assess another chip stock, do not just track headline demand or revenue. Watch whether net margin and absolute profit move in the same direction as the growth story being sold.

What Intel's Recent Run Already Prices In

Intel trades at US$56.28 today after a 47.6% gain over the past year, and the selected Narrative's Fair Value sits below that quote. The Narrative leans on Intel's scale in PCs, servers and AI chips while questioning how far the turnaround can carry manufacturing and product credibility.

The key question now is what must keep going right for that higher price to hold, and the Narrative points squarely at one hurdle a buyer needs to judge: that Intel's push to compress several new process nodes into a short window does not repeat past execution problems while rivals defend their lead.

articles.title: Treasury Rally Gets New Boost as Election Hammers the AI Trade
articles.summary: Wall Street sees the Treasury market emerging as a winner from the Democratic landslide in the US midterm elections, giving traders another reason to rethink...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Wall Street sees the Treasury market emerging as a winner from the Democratic landslide in the US midterm elections, giving traders another reason to rethink this year's sharp selloff.

The party's sweep of Congress was seized upon by bond bulls after tech stocks tumbled on speculation the political shift will tap the brakes on an artificial-intelligence investment boom that's been fueling economic growth, fanning inflation and pushing up interest rates as companies flood the market with debt to finance it.

A politically divided government will also prevent President Donald Trump from passing any major tax or spending bills, easing some of the market's angst about an annual budget deficit that's hit $2 trillion, equivalent to roughly 6% of the economy.

And oil prices tumbled on speculation the Republican defeat will hasten the end of the Iran war, whose energy shock unleashed the bond market selloff eight months ago.

The response to the elections extended a nearly monthlong Treasury rally that pushed 10-year yields down to nearly 4.8%, more than a half-percentage-point below the early October peak. The market largely held its weekly gain even after Friday's Labor Department report showed that job growth accelerated significantly last month.

"AI's been the biggest contributor to nominal GDP, so any kind of stumble probably helps the bond market," said Scott DiMaggio, head of fixed income at AllianceBernstein. "You have the insurance, that if things wobble, we have a great room to move lower in rates."

The bond market's rapid turnaround echoes the one that erupted at the end of 2023, when yields tumbled sharply after the Federal Reserve wrapped up a cycle of interest-rate hikes.

"The macro narrative has shifted following the blue sweep, which investors are taking to mean policy deadlock and less additional deficit spending."

But the scope of the rally has given some analysts pause because the Fed is currently expected resume raising rates next month as inflation continues to run well above its 2% target.

Moreover, the stock market has been dogged by worries about an AI bubble off and on for years, only to rebound as companies keep plowing money into the technology and investors swoop in to buy the dips.

articles.title: Crash Warnings Are Piling Up on Wall Street. Jack Bogle Had a 6-Word Rule for Exactly This.
articles.summary: Four crash warnings in one weekend, a 4.4% drop and the worst week since April. Jack Bogle's rule for moments like this was six words long, and his second ru...
articles.body:
Jack Bogle's rule for a sell-off: "Don't do something, just stand there." A dollar in the S&P 500 fund at the 2007 peak fell to 44 cents by March 2009 and was worth $4.70 on Friday.

His second rule, your age in bonds with Social Security counted as a bond, puts a 70-year-old widow with $1.5 million and $2,900 a month in Social Security near 40/60, not the 70/30 she holds now.

Made inside the IRA the move costs $0 in tax, cuts her loss in a 2007-size fall from $592,974 to $338,842, and leaves $900,000 of bonds paying $43,560 a year, 87% of her spending with Social Security.

Jack Bogle's rule for a week like the one that just ended was six words long: "Don't do something, just stand there." The founder of Vanguard, who launched the first index fund for ordinary investors in 1976 and died in 2019 at 89, said it on CNBC in January 2016 during a global sell-off, had written it in his 2007 book, and repeated the 6-word rule for the rest of his life.

It is worth hearing again this weekend. The S&P 500 finished Friday 6% below its October 6 record after a 4.4% drop on Thursday and its worst week since April, and the crash warnings arrived in a pile: by Sunday afternoon four separate pieces predicting a crash or a bursting bubble sat near the top of the most-read lists, beside a fifth calling Berkshire Hathaway's record $377 billion of cash a warning. Those warnings are a sign of how nervous Wall Street has become after one bad week; they are opinions about what could come next, and none of their authors knows the date, and Bogle did not claim to. When he gave the rule in 2011, as MarketWatch later reported, he added that it was good only about 99% of the time.

articles.title: Gold Holds Decline as US Jobs Data Fan December Rate Hike Bets
articles.summary: Gold held a late-week retreat after strong US jobs data reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will seek to raise interest rates to combat inflation.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Gold held a late-week retreat after strong US jobs data reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will seek to raise interest rates to combat inflation.

Bullion was trading around $4,070 an ounce, after falling 0.4% on Friday. US job growth surged in October and the unemployment rate edged lower, signs of labor-market strength in an expanding economy. Separate data showed US consumer sentiment rose in early November to a three-month high.

Fed officials will see one more jobs report and a full slate of inflation data before their next meeting in December, where they are expected to hike rates as stubbornly high energy prices weigh on prices. Tighter monetary policy is a headwind for gold, which doesn't pay interest.

The precious metal rebounded above the $4,000-an-ounce support threshold after the US midterm elections, as Treasury yields and oil fell on bets that incoming Democrats would push to end the Iran war and a divided government would limit further spending and borrowing. It's still down about a fifth since the US-Iran conflict erupted in late February.

"Gold's post-midterm rollercoaster has brought its two competing forces into sharp focus: its safe-haven appeal remains intact, but the dollar continues to keep a tight lid on its upside," said Hebe Chen, market analyst at Vantage Global Prime.

Traders will look to monthly consumer price index data due Tuesday for the next clues on the path for interest rates. "The CPI report will be the next battleground, testing whether safe-haven demand can muster enough firepower to break through the dollar-driven ceiling," Chen said.

Spot gold slipped 0.1% to $4,065.58 an ounce at 7:35 a.m. in Singapore, while silver fell 0.2% to $51.81. Platinum and palladium edged higher. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, rose 0.4% in the previous session.

articles.title: O que guerras e clima têm a ver com o preço do hambúrguer? | G1
articles.standfirst: Alta dos combustíveis, dos alimentos e dos custos de produção pressiona toda a cadeia do sanduíche; nos Estados Unidos, preço médio do hambúrguer subiu 14% desde 2023, segundo levantamento.
articles.summary: Alta dos combustíveis, dos alimentos e dos custos de produção pressiona toda a cadeia do sanduíche; nos Estados Unidos, preço médio do hambúrguer subiu 14% desde 2023, segundo levantamento.
articles.body:
Hamburguer; lanche — Foto: Jean-claude Attipoe/Unplash

Símbolo do soft power americano durante a Guerra Fria, o hambúrguer é consumido no mundo inteiro, com suas variações regionais, conforme o gosto dos clientes.

Em um mundo sob tensões geopolíticas cada vez mais fortes e com impactos crescentes das mudanças climáticas sobre a produção agrícola mundial, o custo do sanduíche também é uma referência das pressões sobre os preços dos alimentos.

Não à toa, ele se tornou um parâmetro informal da economia, criado há 40 anos pela revista The Economist: o índice Big Mac.

Nos Estados Unidos, o preço do hambúrguer entrou na pauta das eleições parlamentares de meio de mandato, em um contexto de alta da inflação.

💵 Os americanos sentem no bolso os efeitos negativos das guerras sobre os alimentos , mas também dos bloqueios às importações impostos pelo presidente Donald Trump desde que voltou ao poder.

➡️ Entre 2019 e 2024, o valor das ofertas da rede McDonald’s subiu 40% , levando a uma queda de 10% na frequência dos restaurantes entre as populações de menor renda, segundo números da própria empresa.

Em Los Angeles, a reportagem RFI encontrou Andy, que abriu mão das grandes redes na hora do almoço e passou a optar por comerciantes independentes, com valores mais acessíveis.

“Até pouco tempo atrás, nas redes de fast-food, o combo custava US$ 8,99. Agora, no Burger King, sai por quase US$ 18. Isso pesa para mim”, afirma ele.

“Tenho a sorte de a empresa para a qual trabalho pagar a minha gasolina, mas se eu tivesse que arcar com o preço atual do combustível, eu teria que preparar meu almoço em casa e trazer.”

Guerras, energia e cadeia do hambúrguer Um simples hambúrguer envolve uma grande cadeia de produtos e serviços: desde as matérias-primas – trigo, carne, verduras – até a industrialização de ingredientes, como pães e molhos, e das embalagens, sem falar nos transportes.

Rússia e Ucrânia estão entre as maiores exportadoras de cereais do mundo, e a guerra iniciada em 2022 gerou volatilidade nos preços desde então. O conflito também impactou o mercado de fertilizantes agrícolas, que tem na Rússia a principal produtora e exportadora global.

Na sequência, a guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra o Irã fez disparar os preços da energia, com um impacto generalizado na produção de alimentos, salienta Sébastien Abis, especialista em sistemas agrícolas e alimentares e pesquisador associado do Instituto de Relações Internacionais e Estratégicas (IRIS), em Paris.

“Menos petróleo e menos gás são um problema para a agricultura e causam, naturalmente, um aumento nos custos de produção. Cada alta do valor da energia tem repercussões na produção agrícola e em toda a cadeia alimentar, portanto contribuirá para um aumento dos preços para o consumidor, embora essa transferência para o preço final nem sempre seja imediata”, explica.

Clima extremo e segurança alimentar “Devemos temer maiores efeitos sobre a segurança alimentar no próximo ano, principalmente na África e na Ásia, inclusive porque há um fenômeno El Niño se intensificando. Ou seja, temos neste momento uma combinação de choques que precisa ser observada de perto", frisa o especialista.

A empresa Data Essentials criou um índice de preços do hambúrguer. Segundo seus cálculos, o preço médio aumentou 14% desde 2023 nos Estados Unidos, enquanto o da carne bovina no mesmo período subiu mais de 30% – um reflexo da redução dos rebanhos no país, em parte devido ao aumento das secas.

Alguns profissionais aceitam diminuir as margens de lucro para não assustar os seus clientes. Outros distribuem a alta dos preços por todos os itens do cardápio, como batatas fritas ou bebidas. E muitos fazem as duas coisas.

O hambúrguer, consumido nos quatro cantos do planeta, reflete essas tensões em vários outros países.

Na Europa, uma a cada 10 refeições feitas fora de casa é hambúrguer, afirma Maria Bertoch, da consultoria de estudos de mercado de consumo e fast food Circana. Mas, diante da subida dos preços e da ampliação da oferta de outras alternativas mais baratas, como frango frito, as redes do tradicional sanduíche são obrigadas a se adaptar.

Independentes em busca de margem “As marcas otimizam a oferta de produtos, aumentando as opções com frango e vegetarianas, em que elas podem ter maior lucratividade. Também propõem ofertas menores, ao mesmo tempo em que continuam a tentar limitar o aumento do preço daqueles produtos ‘carro-chefe', que atraem os clientes e geram tráfego nos restaurantes”, indica.

Para os independentes, a margem de manobra é mais limitada. O espanhol Madison Smash Burger acaba de conquistar o terceiro lugar no concurso europeu The Champions Burger, disputado em Paris. Mas manter o preço do sanduíche básico a € 13 está cada vez mais difícil, reconhece o cofundador da marca, Christopher Fenelon.

“Todos os custos estão aumentando: carne, pão, realmente tudo está mais caro. Precisamos fazer esforços constantes para nos adaptar”, diz Fenelon. “Nosso negócio está sofrendo com uma situação internacional, mas não podemos aumentar o preço do hambúrguer para € 15 ou € 16, porque ninguém compraria. Nos resta ajustar as margens e apertar o cinto.”

articles.title: Ajuste fiscal: o diagnóstico de organismos internacionais e o desafio de Lula 4 | G1
articles.standfirst: Para romper a atual dinâmica de pressão sobre a inflação, sobre os juros e sobre o endividamento público, a avaliação é de que é necessário fortalecer o quadro fiscal brasileiro.
articles.summary: Para romper a atual dinâmica de pressão sobre a inflação, sobre os juros e sobre o endividamento público, a avaliação é de que é necessário fortalecer o quadro fiscal brasileiro.
articles.body:
Instituições instituições já vêm apontando há anos a necessidade de promover maior sustentabilidade fiscal — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A necessidade de reequilibrar as contas públicas para retomar os superávits primários, reduzir os juros, estimular o crescimento sustentado e, assim, conter o avanço da dívida pública brasileira não é defendida apenas por analistas brasileiros.

Em pronunciamento no domingo (8), o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) disse que preocupa com a trajetória da dívida pública , reafirmou seu compromisso com a responsabilidade fiscal e prometeu criar condições para a redução dos juros, mas não anunciou medidas concretas.

No Brasil, as avaliações de economistas de que um ajuste fiscal mais efetivo seria necessário para melhorar a economia datam antes mesmo do início do terceiro mandato do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , em novembro de 2022, ainda na transição do governo Jair Bolsonaro.

Naquele momento, analistas já julgavam fundamentais medidas mais contundentes de contenção de despesas para compensar a expansão de gastos públicos prevista na chamada Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) da Transição — que ampliou o espaço de gastos em cerca de R$ 170 bilhões por ano.

As recomendações de organismos financeiros internacionais, como o Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI), o banco Mundial (Bird) e o Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento (BID), também não são novidade.

Essas instituições já vêm apontando há anos a necessidade de promover maior sustentabilidade fiscal e, também propondo algumas medidas para conter o avanço do endividamento — que pressiona a taxa de juros.

Reticente sobre a possibilidade de um ajuste mais robusto nas contas públicas, o mercado reagiu negativamente após sua vitória nas eleições. Houve forte queda da Bolsa, alta do dólar e avanço dos juros futuros, enquanto as projeções para a economia se deterioraram.

O que dizem as instituições multilaterais

Para romper a atual dinâmica de pressão sobre a inflação, os juros e o endividamento público, organismos financeiros internacionais avaliam que é necessário fortalecer as contas públicas.

Embora as propostas variem, elas passam principalmente pelo controle do crescimento das despesas, pela revisão de gastos obrigatórios e por reformas que contribuam para estabilizar a dívida pública.

Em julho de 2025, o Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) divulgou documento sobre o chamado "artigo IV", mecanismo de supervisão econômica de seus países-membros.

Naquele momento, observou que economia brasileira registrou um crescimento forte nos últimos três anos, que a inflação cresceu especialmente em 2024 em meio à forte demanda, ao aumento dos preços dos alimentos e à desvalorização da moeda, ultrapassando o intervalo de tolerância da meta.

"Os diretores [do FMI] elogiaram os esforços das autoridades no sentido de continuarem a melhorar a situação fiscal e recomendaram medidas adicionais para colocar a dívida pública numa trajetória descendente sustentada, facilitar uma trajetória da taxa de juros em patamar mais baixo e abrir espaço para investimentos prioritários", dizem, no documento.

O FMI avaliou, também, que medidas destinadas a mobilizar receitas, incluindo a racionalização de gastos tributários ineficientes e o combate à rigidez orçamentária, dariam suporte a estes esforços. "Um quadro fiscal aprimorado com uma forte âncora de médio prazo reforçaria a credibilidade e a sustentabilidade fiscal", acrescentou o organismo internacional.

Em junho do ano passado, o Banco Mundial divulgou o documento “Políticas para Atingir Sustentabilidade Fiscal e Ambiental: Revisão das Finanças Públicas do Brasil”. Nele, avaliou que "déficits fiscais persistentes combinados a baixos níveis de crescimento econômico levaram a um aumento contínuo da dívida pública, o que reforça a necessidade de ajuste fiscal".

A instituição avaliou que os principais fatores por trás do aumento da razão entre dívida e PIB têm sido o aumento das despesas correntes, especialmente com transferências sociais, que beneficiam principalmente o crescente número de brasileiros idosos e concluiu que o país precisaria de um ajuste fiscal na ordem de 3% do PIB para assegurar a sustentabilidade fiscal.

Recomendou cortar benefícios para os mais ricos, ampliando a base tributária do Imposto de Renda da pessoa física ( algo que o governo Lula fez ao contrário, limitando mais a base e se distanciando de países ricos ) e aumentando alíquotas para grandes fortunas e "rendas elevadas", e listou uma série de sugestões de cortes de gastos.

eliminar as regras de indexação e a rigidez das despesas a fim de criar mais espaço no orçamento para as prioridades de políticas públicas;

alinhar os salários do setor público a benchmarks do setor privado;

desvincular as aposentadorias de assistência social e o piso previdenciário do salário-mínimo e adotar um cálculo proporcional para as aposentadorias contributivas com base nos anos de contribuição;

equalizar as idades de aposentadoria e as alíquotas de contribuição previdenciária;

reformar as aposentadorias dos militares, elevando sua alíquota de contribuição e alinhando os benefícios aos de outros regimes;

direcionar o abono salarial para famílias de baixa renda; e

sequenciar a poupança do FGTS a ser utilizada primeiro, antes do acesso ao seguro-desemprego.

Em 2023, o Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento (BID) , chefiado pelo brasileiro Ilan Goldfajn, que presidiu Banco Central no governo de Michel Temer, observou que um nível de endividamento considerado seguro para um país típico da América Latina e Caribe seria de cerca de 46% a 55% do PIB . Atualmente, a dívida brasileira está em 83% do PIB.

O estudo diz que se os níveis de endividamento se tornam demasiadamente altos, ou se a gestão da dívida não é eficaz, as taxas de juros aumentam e o custo do serviço da dívida fica muito oneroso, o que gera consequências ruins: "o investimento e o crescimento sofrem".

Já em novembro de 2024, o BID divulgou sua estratégia para o Brasil até 2027. Nele, a organização avaliou que os desequilíbrios fiscais do Brasil continuam sendo um desafio e observou que a relação dívida/PIB do país já estava entre as mais elevadas da América Latina e do Caribe.

No documento, a instituição multilateral afirma que o fortalecimento do arcabouço fiscal seria essencial para proporcionar melhor proteção social, mantendo ao mesmo tempo a estabilidade macroeconômica e socioeconômica, condição indispensável para um crescimento robusto e sustentado.

E pontua que um dos objetivos estratégicos seria "melhorar a qualidade do gasto público e a sustentabilidade da dívida pública".

"Reformas estruturais são essenciais para enfrentar esse problema e evitar um ajuste fiscal de baixa qualidade que possa penalizar o investimento e prejudicar o bem-estar dos grupos vulneráveis", diz o Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento, em sua análise.

O documento conclui avaliando que o enfrentamento dos desequilíbrios fiscais permitirá ao governo "investir de forma mais eficaz, assegurando o bem-estar de seus cidadãos e abrindo caminho para a prosperidade econômica de longo prazo".

Em 2023, o governo Lula aprovou o arcabouço fiscal , regra que tornou permanente um limite de despesas mais elevado após a PEC da Transição, fixou metas para as contas públicas e permitiu um crescimento real dos gastos de até 2,5% ao ano.

O teto anterior, instituído por Temer e mantido por Jair Bolsonaro, permitia apenas a correção das despesas pela inflação do ano anterior.

Durante o atual governo, a equipe econômica flexibilizou as metas das contas do governo , ampliando o espaço para despesas, fez uso do intervalo de tolerância previsto nas regras para as contas públicas e recorreu a receitas extraordinárias para cumprir os compromissos . Com autorização do Congresso, também realizou despesas por fora do limite estabelecido pela regra fiscal.

Diante do não cumprimento dos compromissos iniciais propostos e do aumento de gastos públicos, as contas do governo passaram os quatro anos do atual governo no vermelho.

Segundo analistas, esse cenário contribuiu para pressionar a inflação, deteriorar as expectativas do mercado, manter os juros em patamar elevado e impulsionar a dívida pública.

articles.title: Robotaxis Aren't Killing Lyft's Business: CEO Says Company Is Growing in AV Markets, Details Waymo Partnership
articles.summary: Lyft Inc. CEO David Risher, during the company’s Q3 2026 earnings call on Thursday, said that autonomous driving and Robotaxis were not impacting the ride-ha...
articles.body:

Lyft Inc. CEO David Risher , during the company's Q3 2026 earnings call on Thursday, said that autonomous driving and Robotaxis were not impacting the ride-hailing company's business in a negative way.

Risher was asked about whether Robotaxis had an impact on Lyft's business in cities like Austin. "I probably won't say too much about any particular market," Risher said. However, the CEO then said that the company was "actually growing" in markets where AVs operate.

"That's really important because it kind of underscores this thesis we've had that AVs are going to be incremental," Risher added. "They're a product people like. Once they get in them, they sort of find after initial hesitation, people find them, they feel safe, they feel very private, and so on and so forth," he said.

However, AV fleets tend to be "small" and "spread out," which leads to longer wait times and other hiccups, he said, which leads to customers switching back to Lyft. "We're continuing to see that, and Austin is no exception to that," the CEO said.

Lyft to Focus Robotaxi Efforts Around Baidu, Waymo

Expanding on Lyft's Robotaxi efforts, Risher said that the company will focus on deepening its partnership with Baidu Inc. 's Apollo Go and Alphabet Inc. 's Waymo . "We're looking for a small number of partners to go deep on. Baidu and Waymo are the two that we're the most focused on right now," he said.

Risher then said that there would be other partners as well, without mentioning who these partners were. He then expanded on Lyft's partnership with Waymo in Nashville, Tennessee, which comprises the "fleet management side" and the "marketplace supply sharing side."

Risher said that the company was expanding its Nashville Waymo fleet "significantly" by the end of 2026. "On the fleet management side, we're operating this 80,000 sq ft facility, which we opened about a month ago. It's going super well," he said, outlining the importance of keeping the vehicles ready for deployment.

Lyft has also partnered with Baidu's Apollo Go to bring autonomous rides to London through its FREENOW platform. Baidu's RT6 robotaxi is currently undergoing safety and validation testing with a safety driver. Risher said the companies are targeting commercial service in 2027.

articles.title: Asian stock markets climb after earlier tech rout
articles.summary: Markets rebound after tech rout triggered by Democrats’ sweeping victory in US midterm elections.
articles.body:
Asian stock markets have rebounded after last week’s tech rout triggered by the Democratic Party’s sweeping victory in the US midterm elections.

Key indexes in Japan, Taiwan and Australia rose on Monday, following a rebound on Wall Street on Friday.

Taipei’s Taiex led the gains, closing up 4.94 percent.

In Tokyo, the benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 2.33 percent, while the S&P/ASX 200 in Sydney edged up 0.099 percent.

In Seoul, the KOSPI fell 0.8 percent after earlier rising about 1.7 percent.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index dipped 0.22 percent.

“We view the recent drawdown in AI infrastructure names as a function of tighter financial conditions, growing scrutiny over credit availability for neocloud companies, and uncertainty over potential delays to the AI build-out post the US midterm election results,” Cameron Chui, Asia equity strategist at JP Morgan Private Bank in Hong Kong, told Al Jazeera.

“That being said, AI demand and adoption remain strong, 2027 capex visibility remains high, and a meaningful valuation reset has already taken place that at least partly factors in these concerns,” Chui added.

“In Asia, we see attractive upside potential in both Taiwan and South Korea, while acknowledging that earnings downside risks have materially risen for 2028, widening the range of potential outcomes.”

Futures for Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 index were up 0.17 percent as of 07:30 GMT, while those tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 were down 0.24 percent.

Futures for both indexes dipped earlier following US-based chip giant Nvidia’s announcement that it would investigate its CEO Jensen Huang over a romantic relationship he had with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Nvidia’s board of directors said that while it had confidence in Huang and had no reason to believe that national security or company secrets were compromised, an independent inquiry would examine “all available information”.

The board said Huang supported the inquiry and pledged his full cooperation.

“The Board prioritises US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said.

The stock market rebound comes after the US midterm results prompted a $2.5 trillion sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday amid concerns that Democratic-controlled legislatures could slow the rollout of data centres used to power artificial intelligence.

The tech rout spilled into Asia on Friday, with the Nikkei 225 and KOSPI plunging about 6 percent and 9 percent, respectively, and the Hang Seng Index dropping more than 1 percent.

The new target suggests an upside of around 12% from the index's last close of 24,986.4.The firm has identified three key factors that could support equities in the coming period: a strong earnings outlook, lower crude oil prices and the possibility of slower capital expenditure on artificial intelligence (AI).Citi has also raised the valuation multiple assigned to the benchmark index.Foreign investors return as AI-linked trades unwindThe revised target comes after a period in which Indian equities lagged their global peers. Enthusiasm around the AI trade and elevated crude oil prices had weighed on the outlook for Indian stocks, particularly as the country is the world's third-largest oil importer.However, the recent market trend has been more encouraging. The Nifty 50 gained more than 10% over seven trading sessions through Friday, supported by renewed buying from foreign portfolio investors (FPIs). The return of foreign money coincided with an unwinding of AI-linked trades and a retreat in oil prices.Citi believes there could be further room for foreign investment in Indian equities."Over the past two years, AI has crowded out almost everything else. Our analysis suggests a ~100bp increase in India active weight could drive ~$12bn of inflows," Citi said in its India equity strategy note dated November 8.FPIs have already purchased Indian shares worth more than $4.1 billion in November so far. This marks their biggest monthly inflows since September 2024.Slower AI spending and lower oil prices improve sentimentThe shift in investor sentiment towards Indian equities has also followed the Democratic victory in the US midterm elections. This fuelled expectations of slower AI-related capital expenditure and lower oil prices, amid hopes of an end to the conflict involving Iran.Citi said the possibility of a slower pace of data centre investments could encourage investors to move towards other assets, potentially benefiting Indian markets."Post US mid-terms, risks of increased pace of data center moratoriums has aided rotation into other assets, (and this) could continue to benefit India," Citi said.Lower crude oil prices are another factor behind the brokerage's positive outlook. Since India is the world's third-largest oil importer, a decline in oil prices could support its macroeconomic outlook as well as earnings assumptions."Lower oil price could help India's macro and earnings assumptions. A $10 (per barrel) lower oil price would help (current account deficit) by 30-40 bps and inflation by 50 bps," the brokerage firm said.Citi raises Nifty's valuation multiple to 18 timesCiti's revised Nifty target also reflects a change in the valuation multiple it uses for the benchmark index. The brokerage has increased its price-to-earnings multiple to 18 times from 17 times, taking its target to 28,000 points by the end of 2027.Its earlier projection had placed the Nifty 50 at 26,000 points by September 2027.The latest estimate therefore reflects both the higher valuation multiple and the brokerage's expectations of support from earnings, lower oil prices and a possible slowdown in AI-related capital expenditure.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. articles.title: Delhi protests: Traders body consider approaching govt, courts over business disruptions
articles.summary: The Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) is considering approaching the government and courts to seek restrictions on protests and demonstrations
articles.body: The Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) is considering approaching the government and courts to seek restrictions on protests and demonstrations that disrupt commercial activity, amid growing concerns among Delhi's traders over losses caused by repeated political agitations.The traders' body will take up the issue at a national meeting in Delhi on November 13, with representatives of trade organisations from across the country expected to attend. It plans to assess the impact of protests in the capital over the past month and draw up a strategy to prevent similar disruptions in other cities.The dispute has gained momentum following a series of demonstrations in Delhi, including the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan. The opposition parties had gathered to protest alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's voter-roll revision exercise and demand the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The issue of protest venues has also been contentious. Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar as the capital's designated protest site on October 11 and identified Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as alternative venues. However, trade organisations have raised concerns about Ramlila Maidan because of its proximity to major wholesale markets in Old Delhi, including Sadar Bazar, Chandni Chowk and Khari Baoli.CAIT has argued that repeated demonstrations, road closures and traffic restrictions affect more than shopkeepers. They disrupt the movement of goods, supply chains, transport services and the livelihoods of employees and small traders. The organisation has said the impact is particularly severe during the festive and wedding seasons, when commercial activity typically picks up.CAIT Secretary General and Chandni Chowk MP Praveen Khandelwal said the organisation would discuss designating suitable locations on city outskirts or other appropriate areas for demonstrations. “The proposed sites would enable peaceful demonstrations while protecting markets, commercial centres, transport routes and essential business activities,” he said, according to a statement.The proposal is aimed at allowing political parties and other groups to exercise their right to protest without affecting the ability of businesses to operate. CAIT has said it wants the arrangement to be considered across the country, rather than being limited to Delhi.The November 13 meeting will also discuss other concerns facing traders, including GST compliance, cyber fraud involving digital payments and the proposed 'One Trader-One Licence' framework. The latter aims to reduce the number of separate licences businesses must obtain from different government departments.CAIT National President B C Bhartia and National Chairman Brij Mohan Agarwal are expected to lead discussions on regulatory changes, simplifying business procedures and strengthening small businesses.The organisation has maintained that the right to peaceful protest must be protected, but should not come at the cost of other citizens' livelihoods and their right to conduct business.You use AI every day. A sustained hold above Rs 143,000-142,600 would be important to maintain the recovery.Gold has rebounded above $4,100/oz, recovering from the previous week’s correction as investors weighed stronger US employment data against softer Treasury yields, a weaker dollar and expectations of easing geopolitical tensions. Spot gold advanced around 0.8% towards $4,104/oz, with the decline in the dollar index providing additional support. However, the latest US labour-market data presented a mixed signal for bullion.October non-farm payrolls increased by 165,000, significantly exceeding market expectations of 65,000, while the unemployment rate declined to 4.1% from 4.2%. The stronger employment reading suggests that the US economy remains relatively resilient, potentially giving the Fed greater flexibility to maintain restrictive monetary conditions.Consequently, expectations of another rate increase in December have strengthened, with markets assigning nearly an 80% probability to a hike. This remains a significant near-term headwind for non-yielding gold, particularly if stronger employment is accompanied by persistent inflation.Nevertheless, softer Treasury yields and dollar weakness have helped bullion recover, highlighting the importance of broader financial conditions alongside interest-rate expectations. Political developments have also influenced market sentiment following Democratic victories in both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections.Markets are reassessing the implications for President Trump’s fiscal and defence spending agenda, government borrowing and broader policy direction. Expectations of greater constraints on additional spending, alongside hopes for diplomatic progress towards ending the Iran conflict, have contributed to lower crude prices and softer Treasury yields, providing some relief to gold.Geopolitical developments surrounding US-Iran relations continue to offer underlying safe-haven support, although any meaningful progress towards de-escalation could reduce immediate defensive demand.At the same time, the ongoing adjustment in global portfolios following the AI-led technology selloff remains a source of volatility, with liquidity requirements and margin-related selling potentially influencing precious-metal positions. Chinese buying and longer-term investment demand could help provide support during corrections.Attention now shifts towards Tuesday’s US CPI release, which will be crucial in determining whether stronger employment is accompanied by renewed inflationary pressure. A higher-than-expected reading could reinforce expectations of a December rate hike, strengthen the dollar and push yields higher, potentially limiting gold’s recovery. articles.title: DLF to invest Rs 3,750 cr in JV with Everstone to buy stake in IREO India
articles.summary: Real estate major DLF and Everstone Group, a Singapore-headquartered global investment manager, will form a JV to invest in IREO pvt ltd and other group
articles.body: Real estate major DLF and Everstone Group, a Singapore-headquartered global investment manager, will form a JV to invest in IREO pvt ltd and other group companies in India (IREO India Companies) held by the IREO group of FDI funds (IREO Funds), with investments from reputed global investors. DLF intends to invest about Rs 3,750 crore for a majority stake in the JV that will hold economic interest in the IREO India companies. The proposed JV intends to invest these funds to acquire at least 20% stake in the IREO India companies, together with certain governance-related rights.Through the proposed transaction, the JV’s aggregate economic interest in the IREO India Companies will be about 40%, with the IREO Funds holding the balance. The proposed transaction could deliver developments across Delhi, Gurugram and other regions. On completion, the IREO India companies will be operated by an independent management team under the guidance of DLF and Everstone.The proposed transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including satisfactory completion of due diligence, receipt of all applicable corporate, regulatory and third-party approvals, and execution of definitive documents. Closing is expected to occur during 2027.DLF MD Ashok Kumar Tyagi said: “We are pleased to partner with everstone group on this strategic investment. Bringing together strong industry experience and global investment capabilities, we look forward to unlocking the growth potential of the IREO India Companies.”Everstone group co-founder and CEO Sameer Sain said: “It’s our privilege to partner with DLF, especially given their incredible capabilities in a market they understand extremely well. Consistent with our fiduciary responsibilities we look forward to working hard and creating significant value for our IREO Funds investors.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Tech firms claw back some losses after midterms rout, eyes on Nvidia
articles.summary: Tech firms clawed back some of last week's losses on Monday fuelled by AI regulation worries, though gains were tempered by news of a probe into Nvidia boss...
articles.body:
Tech firms clawed back some of last week's losses on Monday fuelled by AI regulation worries, though gains were tempered by news of a probe into Nvidia boss Jensen Huang amid claims of an affair with a Chinese spy.

Chipmakers and other companies linked to the artificial intelligence boom took a hammering in the days after Tuesday's US midterms, which saw Democrats sweep both chambers of Congress in a rebuke to Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

The results suggested voters were angry at the president's Iran war and tariffs, which have sent prices soaring, as well as a sharp kickback against the huge data centre buildout that has taken place across the country in recent years.

That has led to speculation the new Congress will seek to wind in tech firms' construction drive, which could put thousands of jobs at risk.

The uncertainty comes with traders already nervous about when the hundreds of billions of dollars pumped into the sector would actually see a profit.

After taking a lashing on Thursday, Wall Street enjoyed a little stability at the end of last week, and Asia -- which had suffered a hammering itself on Friday -- largely followed suit to start this week.

Japan's Nikkei 225 rose more than two percent thanks to gains in Tokyo Electron, Advantest and Sony.

Taipei jumped more than four percent as the Tawainese government pledged support for the market, including curbs on short selling and the back-up of a US$15.2 billion stock stabilisation fund.

There were also gains in Shanghai, Bangkok and Jakarta.

However, Seoul gave up an early rally to end lower, with chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung losing most of their gains. Hong Kong, Wellington, Manila and Mumbai also slipped, while London, Paris and Frankfurt opened lower.

"Investors will be watching carefully this week to get a sense as to whether these gains are just short-covering, bargain hunting or the beginning of something more sustainable in nature," said Sally Auld at National Australia Bank.

"Fears around AI regulation, the outlook for (capital expenditure) and free cash flow have been the driver of risk reduction in recent weeks and these issues are not likely to be resolved with any conviction in the near term.

"Nonetheless, the valuation of many tech stocks now looks less expensive."

However, a little more uncertainty was injected into markets with news that Nvidia's board was launching an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted in a foreign espionage plot following his admission that he was unfaithful to his wife.

articles.title: Global food prices fall in October: Why wheat, dairy and meat are getting cheaper
articles.summary: Global food prices lost some ground in October, with cheaper cereals, dairy products and meat pulling down the overall index despite a sharp rise in sugar
articles.body: Global food prices lost some ground in October, with cheaper cereals, dairy products and meat pulling down the overall index despite a sharp rise in sugar prices. The decline came amid subdued international demand and expectations of higher supplies of some key food commodities, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO).The FAO Food Price Index (FFPI), which measures monthly movements in international prices of a basket of globally traded food commodities, slipped to 133.9 points in October 2026. This marked a decline of 1.6 points, or 1.2%, from the revised September reading.However, the easing in prices has not brought the index below its year-ago level. It was still 5.9% higher than in October last year, although 16.4% lower than its record peak of March 2022.Wheat and maize prices drag down cereal indexCereals recorded one of the steepest declines among the major food categories. The FAO Cereal Price Index dropped 4.5% in October compared with the previous month.Wheat prices reversed their four-month upward trend, with subdued international demand and an improved production outlook, particularly in Argentina, weighing on prices.FAO said “The FAO Cereal Price Index fell 4.5 per cent from September. World wheat prices declined following four consecutive monthly increases, largely reflecting subdued international demand and an improving production outlook, particularly in Argentina”.Expectations that restrictions on Black Sea export flows could ease also put pressure on wheat prices. However, continuing logistical disruptions in the region prevented a sharper decline.Maize prices also softened after touching a three-year high in September. The progress of harvesting in the United States and expectations of ample supplies from major South American exporters contributed to the decline.Rice was an exception within the cereals category. The FAO All Rice Price Index rose 1.6% during October, as harvest delays in some exporting countries and adverse weather conditions pushed prices higher.Dairy and meat prices also move lowerThe decline extended to dairy products, with the FAO Dairy Price Index falling 1.1% from September.Lower international prices of butter and cheese, supported by ample supplies and subdued buying interest, drove the decline. These movements more than offset further increases in milk powder prices.Meat prices followed a similar trend. The FAO Meat Price Index fell 1.2% during the month, although it remained marginally above its level a year earlier.Prices of pig, ovine and bovine meats declined in October, while poultry meat prices remained broadly stable.Sugar bucks the trend, rises to highest level since December 2024Sugar prices continued to move higher even as most other food commodities became cheaper.The FAO Sugar Price Index climbed 6.6% from September and stood 28.8% above its level a year ago. October marked its fourth consecutive monthly increase, taking the index to its highest level since December 2024.Rainfall-related disruptions to sugarcane harvesting and crushing operations in Brazil's key Centre-South region were the main reason behind the increase, FAO said.Concerns about production prospects in India, the European Union and Thailand during the 2026/27 season also added to the upward pressure on prices.Vegetable oil prices edge higherThe FAO Vegetable Oil Price Index recorded a marginal increase of 0.3% in October.Higher prices of soybean and sunflower oils offset the decline in rapeseed oil quotations, leaving the overall index slightly higher than its September level.In a separate assessment, FAO forecast global cereal production at 2,999 million tonnes in 2026. This would make it the second-highest level on record, although it would remain below the record production level achieved in 2025.Global cereal trade is also expected to contract in the 2026/27 season. Trade volumes are projected to fall 3.3% to 507.7 million tonnes, largely due to an expected 8.6% decline in wheat trade.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Huelga general del 11 de noviembre: qué puede y qué no puede hacer tu empresa
articles.standfirst: Claves laborales para organizar la jornada sin vulnerar el derecho de huelga
articles.summary: Claves laborales para organizar la jornada sin vulnerar el derecho de huelga
articles.body: El miércoles 11 de noviembre está convocada una huelga general de 24 horas en toda España, impulsada por CCOO y UGT con reivindicaciones centradas en la vivienda, los salarios y la jornada laboral. Para las empresas, el paro supone un reto organizativo: deben anticipar posibles alteraciones en su actividad, en la atención a clientes y en la relación con proveedores, pero siempre dentro de unos límites legales muy estrictos que protegen un derecho fundamental. La primera regla es no preguntar. La empresa no puede exigir a sus trabajadores que confirmen si van a secundar la convocatoria, ni mediante encuestas ni de manera informal. Lo que sí debe hacer es mantener el centro abierto en su horario habitual y explicar a la plantilla cómo acceder, a quién dirigirse ante cualquier incidencia y cómo justificar retrasos, respetando la libertad de cada persona para trabajar o parar. Conviene documentar y fechar cada decisión organizativa de esos días, porque ante cualquier reclamación será la empresa quien tenga que demostrar que no buscaba frenar la protesta. La ley impide contratar personal externo o recurrir a otros empleados para cubrir los puestos vacantes por la huelga. Tras la sentencia 24/2026 del Tribunal Constitucional, esa prohibición alcanza también a los medios tecnológicos: no se pueden activar automatismos ni adquirir herramientas específicas para neutralizar el paro. Desde CONPYMES advierten de que, para una micropyme, la jornada puede traducirse en un cierre forzoso, y recomiendan afrontarla desde el diálogo y la legalidad. Quien haga huelga perderá el salario del día, junto con la parte proporcional del descanso semanal y de las pagas extraordinarias. Durante ese tiempo no hay obligación de cotizar: el trabajador pasa a situación de alta especial, que la empresa debe comunicar a la Tesorería General a través del Sistema RED. El registro de jornada será la prueba objetiva de las ausencias. Además, si alguien no puede trabajar por causas ajenas a su voluntad, ese tiempo debe retribuirse.

articles.title: Nvidia shares drop after CEO Jensen Huang admits affair with suspected Chinese spy; what it means for company
articles.summary: Nvidia shares declined in after-hours trading on Monday following the announcement of an internal investigation to find out if the company’s chief
articles.body: Nvidia shares declined in after-hours trading on Monday following the announcement of an internal investigation to find out if the company’s chief executive Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The investigation has raised questions about Jensen Huang’s future at the AI chipmaker which is among the most valuable listed companies in the world.Announced on Sunday, the investigation has drawn attention to Huang's position at Nvidia, the world's most valuable chipmaker. His future is also under scrutiny because of his prominent role as one of the leading salesmen of the artificial intelligence boom.Jensen Huang, 63, has headed Nvidia since he established the company in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. His long tenure makes him one of Silicon Valley's longest-serving chief executives among company founders.Born in Taiwan and brought up in the US, Huang emerged as a key figure in the artificial intelligence revolution. He steered Nvidia from its original business of manufacturing graphics chips for video games to becoming the world's leading supplier of AI processors.Jensen Huang & the 'Chinese spy' scandalThe company launched the internal inquiry following a media report alleging that Huang had a close association with a Chinese businesswoman who had allegedly shared information with Beijing. In a message to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged that he had been unfaithful to his wife but did not provide details about the relationship.The New York Times reported last month that Huang had been involved in a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed who is not related to him. US authorities investigated Alice Huang and concluded that she was an asset of Chinese intelligence.Megaspeed's website identifies the company as an Nvidia Cloud Partner in the Asia-Pacific region. It also lists Nvidia's GB200 NVL72 and HGX H100 chips among the products it offers.The developments also had repercussions in South Korea. Madison Huang, Jensen Huang's daughter and an Nvidia executive, called off a scheduled visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference due to begin on Monday, according to companies that had been due to meet her.Madison Huang had been scheduled to visit South Korean artificial intelligence startup Rebellions and participate in a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said both engagements had been called off because of "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia."South Korean media reported that Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day conference expected to attract around 2,000 participants, would go ahead as scheduled. The event is set to focus on physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Impact on Nvidia and its sharesAccording to a Reuters report, trading in perpetual futures on the Hyperliquid exchange, along with after-hours share transactions on the Blue Ocean system, indicated that Nvidia shares were changing hands at around $178.60. This is a decline of more than 4% from the stock's closing price of $186.64 on the Nasdaq on Friday.Nvidia's chip technology has played a central role in several major shifts in the technology industry, spanning video gaming, autonomous vehicles, cloud computing and artificial intelligence.Huang's early decision to invest in AI proved significant. By the time ChatGPT was launched in late 2022, Nvidia's processors were already central to the computing infrastructure needed to meet the rapidly growing demand for AI applications.The company's market value has since climbed sharply, making it one of the world's most valuable businesses and an essential supplier to leading technology companies. Nvidia's valuation rose from $420 billion in late 2022 to $4.5 trillion as of November 6."The market's probably telling you now this does no favours ⁠to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build out of data centres," Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne told Reuters.However, Weston said he did not expect Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", to be replaced."If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down — it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest,” he said.The scrutiny of Huang's relationship with Alice Huang has emerged at a sensitive point for Nvidia. Investors are already questioning whether the AI boom that fuelled the company's extraordinary growth can be sustained. The board's investigation has added another layer of uncertainty by raising questions about the future of the executive most closely linked to Nvidia's success.The issue has also drawn attention from senior Republicans in the US House of Representatives, who have sought briefings from Huang following The New York Times report, pointing to concerns over national security.Nvidia has maintained that its board has "no reason to believe" that US national security or company secrets were compromised. However, an independent committee of directors will examine all the information available as part of its review.Analysts cautioned that an extended investigation or internal review could affect Nvidia's investment decisions and product launches, potentially creating wider repercussions for the semiconductor industry.Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, said competitors such as Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) could receive increased attention in the near term. This could also bring Samsung into greater focus because of its close business ties ⁠with AMD.However, Ryu said Nvidia's products would be difficult to replace, which could limit the overall impact of the developments. He added that shipments to China might face further delays, depending on how the situation unfolded.South Korea's deputy science minister said on Monday that the government did not expect any disruption to deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units covered by existing contracts, despite the challenges currently confronting the company.Shares of Nvidia's major Asian chip suppliers recovered on Monday following last week's selloff in AI-related stocks. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) rose 6.5%, while Samsung Electronics gained 2.9% and SK Hynix advanced 4.7%.Several prominent personalities also commented on Huang's admission. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, who founded Pershing Square Capital Management, described the Nvidia chief executive as an "incredible human" in a post on X. However, he added that ‌if "indeed this is ⁠more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem.""I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security," he added.Tesla CEO Elon Musk responded with "I agree" to a post by Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire. Maguire had said Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that was "bad for America", while also maintaining that "Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership".US President Donald Trump said on Sunday that he had not discussed the allegations with Huang. He nevertheless described the Nvidia CEO as a fine person. "I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job," he added.Asked whether he believed he should have acted on the intelligence after being briefed about it, Trump said: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for ⁠it. You have to hear it."The New York Times reported that Trump had been briefed on the intelligence findings approximately a year ago but decided against taking action based on the information.You use AI every day. articles.body: US stock futures rose on Monday as the AI trade remained in focus ahead of a busy week of earnings and inflation data.Futures on the Dow Jones Industrial Average (YM=F) rose 0.8%, while those on the S&P 500 (ES=F) gained 0.3%. Contracts for the Nasdaq-100 (NQ=F) rose just above the flatline after all three indexes posted losses last week.All eyes will be on how the artificial intelligence trade opens on Monday following a volatile post-election shake-up in markets and the revelation that Nvidia's (NVDA) board is opening an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over his affair. articles.title: ‘Will have to return deposits’: Musk says Tesla will end Cybertruck production, rejects unprofitability claims
articles.summary: Tesla will have to refund deposits to a large number of customers who placed orders for its Cybertruck pickup, as demand has outstripped the company's
articles.body: Tesla will have to refund deposits to a large number of customers who placed orders for its Cybertruck pickup, as demand has outstripped the company's production capacity, CEO Elon Musk said. The electric vehicle maker plans to wind down production of the model at its Texas factory in about eight months to make room for its autonomous Cybercab.“We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months, but will have to return deposits for a lot of people,” Musk said in a post on X on Monday, acknowledging that the Cybertruck's order rate was significantly higher than its production rate.Further rejecting unprofitability rumours, he added, "This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production."The latest comments follow Musk's announcement last week that Tesla would add an extra production shift to clear outstanding Cybertruck orders before ending production. The manufacturing line is expected to be shut down around mid-2027, with resources redirected towards scaling up Cybercab output.Musk has rejected suggestions that the decision to discontinue the pickup was driven by profitability concerns. He argued that the complexity of manufacturing the Cybertruck made expanding its production less valuable than using the capacity to build more Cybercabs.“This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media, but rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production,” he said.Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and began customer deliveries in November 2023. Despite Musk's ambitious sales projections, the pickup has struggled to attract the expected demand. US sales fell 48 per cent to 20,237 units last year, according to Kelley Blue Book, far below Musk's earlier projection of annual sales reaching 250,000 vehicles.The Cybercab, unveiled in October 2024, is a two-seater autonomous electric vehicle designed without a steering wheel or pedals. articles.title: Nvidia's out-of-hour shares fall as firm probes CEO Jensen Huang

articles.body:
By Heekyong Yang, Kyu-seok Shim and Tom Westbrook

SEOUL/SYDNEY, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Nvidia ( NVDA ) stock fell 4% during premarket trading on Monday after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.

The internal probe followed a media report that Huang had a close ‌relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who allegedly passed information to Beijing. Huang told Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship.

The ‌investigation, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

The fallout extended to South Korea, where Madison Huang, Huang's ​daughter and an Nvidia executive, cancelled a planned visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference that was set to begin on Monday, according to companies she had been scheduled to meet.

Perpetual futures trading on the Hyperliquid exchange and after-hours shares trading on the Blue Ocean system showed Nvidia prices around $180.30 a share, down about 3.4% from Friday's Nasdaq closing price of $186.64.

"The market's probably telling you now this does no favours to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build out of data centres," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.

But Weston said he did ‌not think Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", would be ⁠replaced.

"If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down — it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest," he said.

The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated ⁠and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Singapore.

Alice Huang did not respond to the New York Times last month when it first reported her relationship with Huang, and Reuters could not determine her location to seek comment on Monday.

Shares in Nvidia's key Asian chip suppliers TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rebounded on Monday after last week's selloff ​of ​AI-related stocks. TSMC shares jumped 6.5%, while those in Samsung and SK Hynix climbed 2.9% and 4.7%, respectively.

articles.title: Jensen Huang just handed Wall Street its first $4.5 trillion CEO scandal
articles.summary: Wall Street has priced plenty of CEO scandals. It has never priced one at a company worth $4.5 trillion that makes up nearly 7% of the S&P 500.
articles.body:
Wall Street has priced plenty of CEO scandals. It has never priced one at a company worth $4.5 trillion that makes up nearly 7% of the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ).

Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang admitted in a Nov. 8 memo to employees to an affair with Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials believe worked for China's Ministry of State Security. "I was unfaithful to my wife," he wrote. The board has opened an independent investigation.

Nvidia stock fell 5% before the bell on Monday following the news.

The scale is hard to overstate. At Friday's close, Nvidia was worth about four times the nine biggest companies ever hit by CEO personal-conduct scandals combined, by Yahoo Finance calculations. The largest, Intel ( INTC ), was worth $249 billion when Brian Krzanich resigned in 2018 over a past consensual relationship with an employee. Nvidia is about 18 times that.

This is key-person risk — the danger that a company's value rests on one person — at its most extreme. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has run it ever since, with no named successor.

Adjust for a bigger stock market, and the gap narrows but doesn't close. No earlier scandal-hit company made up more than about 1% of the S&P 500, a mark only Intel in 2018 and HP ( HPQ ) in 2010 reached. Nvidia is about seven times that.

History puts a price on it. A 2018 study in the Journal of Financial Economics found stocks fell about 4% on average when the CEO was the one caught. At Nvidia's size, that's roughly $185 billion, more than McDonald's ( MCD ) was worth when it fired Steve Easterbrook in 2019.

So far, Wall Street has treated Nvidia like the safe chip stock.

Since Oct. 28, the last close before The New York Times' first spy report, Nvidia has fallen about 13%. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) is down about 20% in a stretch that included a post-midterm rout. The gap holds from Nvidia's Oct. 6 record too.

Spy stories can hit hard. Super Micro Computer ( SMCI ) lost 41% in a day in 2018 on a report of Chinese spy chips in its servers, a report that was never confirmed.

The closer precedent may be Intel's Lip-Bu Tan. In August 2025, President Trump said Tan should resign over his China ties [1p link?]. Within a month, Washington had taken a stake in Intel and the stock was up about 20%.

This time, Trump is in the CEO's corner. "I think he's an honorable guy," he told reporters Sunday.

Options traders were braced even before the admission. Friday's prices implied a move of more than 3% either way for Monday alone, more than double Nvidia's typical day lately.
